findings.title: Successful cleanup batches are logged as errors
findings.body: The new cleanup logging emits Error messages unconditionally, even when ID selection and deletion succeed or there is nothing to delete. The same pattern appears in count-based cleanup and orphaned-tag cleanup. Consequently, normal background maintenance produces error-level logs every cycle, triggering log-based alerts and obscuring genuine failures; logging every selected ID also makes these messages unnecessarily large. Use debug-level summary logging for successful work and reserve error-level logging for actual failures.

findings.title: SQLite ID-list construction copies the entire prefix for every ID
findings.body: For SQLite batches larger than 999, each iteration formats the accumulated values string into a new string. Building a batch of N IDs therefore requires quadratic copying and allocation rather than linear work. Large configured batches, such as the 32767 batch size introduced in the tests, can allocate gigabytes of temporary strings during cleanup, causing substantial GC and CPU overhead in the server. Build the list with a strings.Builder or an append-based buffer instead.
